name: Historic Sandstone Masonry (Red/Yellow/Buff Sandstone)
traditional_use: Primary structural ashlar blocks, retaining wall facades, pillars, beams, brackets, and steps in Vavs, Baolis, and Bawaris across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and UP.

moisture_behavior.breathability: Moderate vapor permeability along natural bedding planes
moisture_behavior.capillary_suction: Active capillary suction drawing moisture from damp foundation soils
moisture_behavior.drying_rate: Moderate drying rate dependent on surface air circulation and open joints
moisture_behavior.summary: Porous natural stone that relies on breathable lime joints to evaporate absorbed groundwater.

mechanical_characteristics.stiffness: Moderate stiffness with anisotropic behavior along sedimentary bedding planes
mechanical_characteristics.ductility: Quasi-brittle in tension; vulnerable to edge spalling when subjected to point loads
mechanical_characteristics.sacrificial_behavior: Primary historic substrate; must NEVER be sacrificed to save joint mortar
mechanical_characteristics.summary: Strong in compression, but highly susceptible to edge fractures if bound with overly stiff modern cement.

thermal_characteristics.thermal_shock_resilience: Good resistance to uniform diurnal heating
thermal_characteristics.summary: Differential expansion occurs when covered by materials with differing thermal coefficients.

chemical_considerations.ph_nature: Neutral to slightly acidic depending on silica vs calcium carbonate matrix cementation
chemical_considerations.soluble_salts_risk: Highly vulnerable to salt crystallization decay (sub-florescence) from trapped sulfates
chemical_considerations.reactivity_with_limestone: Chemically stable in contact with lime; reacts destructively with alkaline cements
chemical_considerations.summary: Trapped salts in sandstone pores exert crystallization pressures up to 50-100 MPa, causing granular disintegration.

reversibility.extraction_method: Permanent historic fabric to be conserved in situ

heritage_compatibility.iks_alignment: Core indigenous building material shaped by master stone carvers (Sompuras/Silawats)
heritage_compatibility.asi_intach_compliance: Protected historic fabric under Indian Ancient Monuments Act

limitations: Quarry provenance (Dholpur, Jodhpur, Dhrangadhra, Khatu) dictates pore structure and compressive strength.
Petrographic thin-section analysis is required to determine whether cementation is siliceous, ferruginous, or calcareous.
